title: The unmatched 3%
prompt: 97% of the wiki's users have emails that match SSO. 3% are legacy contractor accounts with personal emails that do not exist in SSO. Several restricted pages list those contractors. What do you propose?

options.text: Make pages that name unmatched users visible to everyone for now.
options.feedback: Never index sensitive content with an allow-all ACL for now. That turns an identity gap into an exposure.

options.text: Replace group ACLs with flattened user lists to catch everyone.
options.feedback: Flattening does not fix unmatched identities, and flattened lists drift. Map groups directly.

options.text: Reference users by email, document the unmatched 3%, and agree a customer-approved manual map or exclusion.
options.feedback: Right. Email references fit a shared identity provider. Without identity data for the rest, a manual map to corporate identities is needed, or those accounts get no access.

takeaway: Unmatched identities get a decision, never a broad ACL.
